Dealer Selling Restored 1957 Bel Air That Hides Just Two Reasons To Make Buyers Walk Away
73 photos
Photo: Drive the Coast on eBay
1957 continues to be one of the most desirable model years in the history of the Bel Air, and this specimen shows exactly why. While the car has already been restored, so it now presents in immaculate condition, I can’t help but admire those beautiful lines, the fantastic cabin, and the chrome that perfectly highlights the gorgeous design of old-school classics.
That’s why I believe this Bel Air won’t remain up for grabs for too long. The dealer selling the car explains the convertible doesn’t need anything, and you can tell this is true by simply checking out the photos in the gallery.
The paint is absolutely amazing, and I feel that the photos don’t do enough justice to this Bel Air. You should probably see it in person to admire this Bel Air from every angle, so call the dealer and do yourselves a favor and go there to see this car with your own eyes.
Photo: Drive the Coast on eBay There is basically no reason to ignore a 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air when it presents in this kind of condition. This isn’t just a beautiful car but also an iconic model that has now become one of the most recognizable in the history of American classics.
The 1957 model year was the last release of the Tri-Five, so it’s naturally a highly desirable collectible that can cost more than you can imagine when checking the right boxes.
While Ford continued to dominate the American car space, the battle was now fiercer than ever, especially as Chevrolet continued to insist on V8 power and luxurious cars. The 1957 Bel Air had both these main focuses, as it wasn’t only a luxurious presence on the road, with a flood of chrome and other exquisite touches exclusive to this top-of-the-line Chevy configuration, but also a more powerful car.
The 1957 model year witnessed the introduction of the 283 Turbo-Fire. If you believe you’ve seen this engine somewhere else, it’s because you had, as this Turbo-Fire ended up making its way to most Chevrolet models produced throughout the ‘60s.
The 283 was based on the 265 that was already available on the Bel Air since earlier in the same decade, but this time, Chevrolet was ready for massive power. It started with a two-barrel configuration and was configured with more powerful setups that included the famous Corvette engines and a fuel-injected variant that produced 283 horsepower when fitted with solid lifters.
Photo: Drive the Coast on eBay A 283 is also installed under the hood of this 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air. The V8 power is exactly what it needed to become a collectible, as a six would have certainly reduced its customer appeal.
I’m pretty sure that you’re looking for those two reasons to walk away that I mentioned in the headline. The car was restored as close to factory specifications as possible, and these two reasons are the exceptions to this ambitious objective.
The aluminum radiator and the electric cooling fan, which, according to the dealer, have been added for “improved drivability,” are the only non-factory-correct parts on this Bel Air. Everything else should align with Chevrolet’s expectations, including the body, the engine, and the chrome.
The Gypsy Red paint looks spotless, and there’s no doubt this is also the case when you have the car in front of your eyes. The vehicle has properly been babied since the moment the restoration was finalized, and there’s absolutely no doubt that this should also be the case once it finds a new home. Parking it in a heated garage is the only way to care for this collectible.
The engine is paired with a 3-speed automatic transmission, and while no additional specifics have been offered, it’s safe to assume that it doesn’t need a single repair. The car should be ready for the road, and if you just want to hop in and drive, you should be able to do this.
Photo: Drive the Coast on eBay Let’s talk money.
I don’t think you need to be a die-hard restoration guy or a Chevrolet fanboy to figure out the price. This is an expensive car, and the frame-off restoration is a sign that you won’t be able to get it for pocket money.
The dealer is selling this car at auction, with the starting bid set at $39,000. However, a reserve is also in place, and that makes perfect sense, as you won’t be able to buy the car this cheap. The dealer did not reveal any information related to the reserve, so it is safe to assume that it’s close to the Buy It Now price configured at $130,000.
This is also the price you have to pay for the car if you want to avoid the digital fight. The auction ends in 4 days, and if you want to see the Bel Air in person, you must pack your bags for a quick trip to Santa Rosa Beach, Florida.
